title: Isolated Handoff Protocol and Telemetry Fabrics for Dedicated & Private Inference
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, authenticated handoff protocol and telemetry fabric that enables Dedicated and Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments to stream traces, metrics, and logs into Redwood's central observability plane while preserving tenant isolation, provenance guarantees, and low tail latency.

Background: Private deployments currently use a mix of sidecars and perimeter forwarders with ad‑hoc semantics for trace IDs and sampling. We need a standardized handoff that: (1) prevents cross‑tenant mixing when collectors aggregate, (2) preserves an opaque provenance chain for forensics without leaking customer identifiers, and (3) provides adaptive buffering and backpressure to maintain SLOs under bursty inference workloads.

Scope: Design and implement the handoff protocol with: authenticated envelopes, monotonic per‑tenant sequence markers, optional signed provenance attestations, adaptive buffering policy at the edge, and a small runtime shim that normalizes headers for central ingestion. Build corresponding ingestion adapters (Kafka/HTTP) and dashboarding hooks for latency/error and sampling drift.

Non‑goals: Full rewrite of existing collector fleet or replacement of customer sidecar; deep storage/retention policy changes (handled by separate retention workstream).

Success criteria:
- Central ingestion can attribute and surface telemetry from Dedicated/VPC clusters without any cross‑tenant spans observed in test harness (end‑to‑end test).
- 99th percentile telemetry ingestion latency for trace events <= 400ms under 4x baseline traffic in staging.
- No PII or raw customer IDs present in central logs when provenance mode = opaque (verified by automated scrubber and audit run).
- Rollout strategy enabling opt‑in on a per‑customer basis and safe fallback to current perimeter forwarder in case of failure.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Security and Infra (PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1428)
Integration test demonstrating isolated ingestion for 3 simulated tenants with synthetic burst traffic (results in CI)
Dashboard widget in Console showing per‑route ingestion latency and error rate for Private/Dedicated origins
Automated audit that confirms no customer identifiers emitted when provenance mode=opaque
Feature flag and rollback playbook documented in runbook for on‑call teams
comments: 2025-02-10 Riley Chen: Initial ticket created after infra design review. Captured high‑level requirements from AE and two enterprise customers asking for stronger isolation guarantees for VPC deployments.

2025-02-14 Priya Kapoor: Spiked a prototype for signed envelopes; discovered HMAC approach is sufficient for attestations (handles rotation via KMS). Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood/telemetry-envelope-proto

2025-02-18 Marco Nguyen (Security): Reviewed envelope prototype. Recommendation: include non‑replay nonce + tenant sequence marker. Also require opt‑in provenance flag per org in control plane. Security review kickoff scheduled.

2025-02-21 Eng Sync: Decided tradeoffs: full per‑span signing is too expensive; we'll sign batches and include monotonic seq markers per tenant. This preserves forensic chainability without per‑span crypto overhead.
2025-02-25 Priya Kapoor: Implemented edge shim that normalizes headers (x-rwd-tenant-hash, x-rwd-seq) and supports buffering/backpressure. Benchmarks in staging show 95th latency for shim < 6ms.

2025-03-01 SRE Review: Verified adaptive buffering policy works with current collector fanout. Noted a corner case where long GC pauses on older JVM nodes could cause temporary seq gaps; follow up task created to add durable local write‑ahead buffer for JVM hosts.

2025-03-04 Riley Chen: Drafted rollout plan: start with Canary customers in Dedicated clusters (customers flagged in control plane), enable opaque provenance mode, monitor Console dashboards for a week, then widen to Private VPCs. Rollback involves disabling handoff and reconfiguring perimeter forwarder mapping.

2025-03-04 Priya Kapoor: Open PRs: https://github.com/redwood/collector-adapters/pull/256, https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/881 — contain ingestion adapter and dashboard panels respectively. Code review requested from @mateo and @linh.
